key_insight: SynPre-FL combines privacy-preserving synthetic EHR pretraining with federated learning to improve robustness on heterogeneous clinical prediction tasks.
clinical_relevance: The framework may help hospitals build risk-prediction models from distributed patient data without centralizing records, while improving reliability and interpretability.
method: Latent autoencoder-diffusion model generates high-fidelity synthetic EHR cohorts.
Synthetic data are used to warm-start federated training across non-IID clients.
Training adds class-balanced local objectives, proximal regularization, adaptive aggregation, and post-hoc calibration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports preserved statistical structure, resistance to membership-inference and reconstruction attacks, strong TSTR/TRTS utility, and improved performance across 5, 10, and 15 heterogeneous clients.
watch_item: Real-world deployment may still depend on the fidelity, governance, and external validation of the synthetic generator across different hospitals and EHR schemas.
paper_title: SynPre-FL: Synthetic data-driven pretraining integrated Federated Learning training framework
